subject: Order form: activation fee split, invoicing cadence, and tax evidence
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@hearthtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: activation fee split, invoicing cadence, and tax evidence

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We pushed a draft of the Order Form and one-page commercial schedule into the SharePoint folder; attaching the redline you sent with our in-line comments. A few items we want to confirm before legal finalizes:

- Activation / onboarding fee: HearthTech requested the fee be invoiced 50% up front, 50% on go-live. Our standard is 100% at signing for activation. We can do 50/50 if the activation portion is limited to professional services hours (see table).
- Minimum commit: the draft shows a 12-month minimum of $180k. We are open to a quarterly tranching schedule, but need clarity on invoice sequence to avoid backlog when credits apply.
- Net terms: Redwood standard is Net 30. Procurement referenced Net 45 in their comment — please confirm whether Net 30 is a blocker for you.
- Taxes & evidence: Procurement asked whether HearthTech can accept self-certification on VAT/residency and provide a tax certificate prior to the first invoice. Our finance team will need either a W-9 (US) or VAT registration evidence (EU).

Next steps I propose: if you can confirm acceptable net terms and the activation invoice split, Ben can circulate a limited set of legal redlines (commercial only) and we’ll route to DocuSign the same day. If procurement needs formal tax forms, point us to the mailbox and we’ll exchange securely.

Short timeline preference from our side: get commercial sign-off this week so we can begin provisioning next Monday.

Thanks —
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0107
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@hearthtech.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@hearthtech.com>, Peter Smith <peter.smith@wilsonharrislaw.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: activation fee split, invoicing cadence, and tax evidence

Tessa — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick answers from HearthTech:

- Activation fee: 50/50 split is acceptable provided the go-live milestone is strictly defined (we will add an acceptance sign-off).
- Minimum commit: the $180k annual is fine; we prefer quarterly invoices (approx $45k) with a reconciliation after Q2.
- Net terms: Net 45 is what Procurement requires for enterprise vendors. We can do Net 30 if Redwood is willing to accept a 1.5% prompt payment fee for Net 30.
- Taxes: We will provide the VAT registration (we are EU-registered) and can upload the certificate to the secure folder. Peter (cc) will coordinate legal redlines for the Order Form and MSA reference.

Please proceed with Ben’s redlines on the commercial appendix and we’ll review. Our target is to sign the Order Form by end of week.

Olivia
VP Finance, HearthTech
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@hearthtech.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: activation fee split, invoicing cadence, and tax evidence

Olivia — appreciate the quick clarity. I’m attaching two items: 1) a one-page commercial amendment that captures the 50/50 activation, quarterly invoice cadence, and the prompt payment alternative; 2) an invoice schedule template so both teams can confirm line timing.

Commercial notes:
- If HearthTech requires Net 45, Redwood would prefer the minimum commit be invoiced in equal quarterly installments with a reconciliation credit applied at the annual anniversary (no retroactive refunds).
- Prompt payment option: Net 30 with a 1.5% discount applied if paid within 15 days. This would preserve Redwood’s cash flow without blocking procurement.
- Tax evidence: we will accept the VAT certificate; please upload to the secure folder and notify finance@redwood.ai. Finance will attach the certificate to the first invoice metadata.

Peter — looping you so your redline can focus on the two commercial bullets above and the defined go-live acceptance clause. We are not changing the MSA aside from cross-references to the Order Form Schedules.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Invoice_Schedule_v2.xlsx, Commercial_Amendment_1p.pdf
From: Peter Smith <peter.smith@wilsonharrislaw.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@hearthtech.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HearthTech Order Form redlines (v3)

Forwarding the redline from our counsel and a short note: please see in-line edits in HearthTech_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx — primary asks from HearthTech legal are:

- Clarify invoice application when credits exist (procurement wants credit to apply against next invoice, not extend terms).
- Add explicit tax gross-up language for withholding taxes (HearthTech is asking for a reciprocal tax treatment).
- Strengthen the go-live acceptance language: 5-business-day review window after deployment, otherwise acceptance is deemed.

Ben — the redline marks a couple of alternative phrasing for the prompt-payment discount; we recommend Redwood accept the Net 30 + 1.5% early pay discount instead of Net 45. If you can agree, we’ll remove the alternative bracketed language and circulate final.

Peter
Senior Counsel, Wilson Harris LLP

Attachment: HearthTech_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@hearthtech.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Peter Smith <peter.smith@wilsonharrislaw.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: activation fee split, invoicing cadence, and tax evidence

Team — quick update from Redwood finance/legal: we can accept the following as final commercial positions:

- Activation fee: 50/50 (50% at signing, 50% at go-live). Go-live acceptance language to be: deploy -> 5 business day review -> deemed accepted if no documented rejection.
- Invoice cadence: quarterly equal installments for the minimum commit with reconciliation at anniversary. Credits apply to the next invoice, not to extend payment terms.
- Net terms & prompt payment: we will accept Net 30 with the 1.5% early payment discount (applies if payment received within 15 days) in lieu of Net 45.
- Taxes: we will accept the VAT certificate upload. Redwood finance will request the certificate before issuing the first invoice; if withholding applies, we’ll follow the reciprocal tax gross-up language in the redline.

Ben — please incorporate Peter’s cleaned redline and the invoice schedule into a single Order Form that we can route for signatures. Olivia — once the final doc is uploaded I’ll send the DocuSign request and finance will begin the onboarding billing profile.

Thanks —
Tessa
